raw_response:
I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life, just like my father before me. I have about 10 mu. There's really only one way to farm here — winter wheat, then summer corn. Everyone does it. The land doesn't rest; neither do I.

For wheat, I'll plant after the corn harvest in mid-October. I'll use Jimai 22 — it's what the county ag store recommends and my neighbors have had good results with it. I'll rotary-till before planting to break up the compacted soil. I'll put down compound fertilizer as a base, then top-dress with urea at jointing. I need to water at least three times — before winter, at jointing, and at heading. If I skip the jointing irrigation the yield drops badly. I'll spray herbicide early, then fungicide around heading for powdery mildew. Hoping for 450 jin per mu.

For corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no time to spare. Hybrid seed is the only way — the old varieties can't compete. I don't till for corn, just plant directly into the stubble with a seeder I borrow from my cousin. I'll apply fertilizer twice — at planting and when the stalk is knee-high. Two irrigations if the summer rains are weak. I'll spray for corn borer once. I expect about 550 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

Water is getting harder every year — the well is deeper than when I was young — but I don't see a way around it.
